name: Rosuvastatin + Clopidogrel
meta: Rosuvastatin Calcium: C10AA07; Clopidogrel Bisulphate: B01AC04
Schedule H – prescription only; Clopidogrel Bisulphate: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White amorphous powder (calcium salt), sparingly soluble in water.
321.82 g/mol (base); 419.9 g/mol (bisulfate; 97.875 mg bisulfate ≈ 75 mg base)
White to off-white powder (bisulfate), practically insoluble in water at neutral pH.

Rosuvastatin Calcium: The JUPITER trial (2008) showed a 44% reduction in major CV events in people with normal LDL but raised hs-CRP. Generics available from 2016. First approval/introduction: Discovered by Shionogi; patented 1991; US FDA August 2003 (AstraZeneca). Clopidogrel Bisulphate: CAPRIE (1996) showed modest benefit over aspirin in atherosclerotic disease; CURE (2001) established dual antiplatelet therapy in non-ST-elevation ACS. First approval/introduction: Patented 1982; US FDA 1997 (Sanofi and Bristol-Myers Squibb).
Combines lipid lowering and plaque stabilisation with platelet inhibition, the two pillars of atherothrombotic secondary prevention, improving adherence via a single daily dose.

Rosuvastatin Calcium Competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis; up-regulates hepatic LDL receptors, lowering LDL-C (up to ~55% at 20 mg), triglycerides and raising HDL-C. Pleiotropic plaque-stabilising effects. Receptor / target profile: Potent competitive HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; hydrophilic and hepatoselective (OATP1B1 uptake).

Clopidogrel Bisulphate Prodrug activated by CYP2C19 to a metabolite that irreversibly blocks the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor, inhibiting ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation for the platelet's lifespan. Receptor / target profile: Prodrug whose active metabolite irreversibly blocks the P2Y12 ADP receptor for the life of the platelet.
Limited (~10%), mainly CYP2C9 to N-desmethyl rosuvastatin
Summary: Bioavailability ~20%; Tmax 3–5 h. ~90% protein bound. Minimal metabolism (CYP2C9). Half-life ~19 h. Mainly faecal excretion. Asian patients have ~2-fold higher exposure.
Hepatic – ~85% esterase hydrolysis to inactive acid; ~15% two-step CYP2C19/3A4/2B6/1A2 activation to thiol active metabolite
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; Tmax ~0.75 h. ~85% hydrolysed to inactive acid; ~15% activated via CYP2C19 (two-step). Half-life of parent ~6 h; antiplatelet effect lasts 5–7 days.
Secondary prevention in patients with established atherosclerotic disease (recent MI, ischaemic stroke, peripheral arterial disease) and dyslipidaemia
Acute coronary syndrome (after loading) with dyslipidaemia
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use with caution in moderate disease.
Active liver disease or unexplained persistent raised transaminases
Pregnancy and lactation; women of child-bearing potential not using contraception
Active pathological bleeding (peptic ulcer, intracranial haemorrhage)
Myopathy/rhabdomyolysis – report muscle pain; check CK; higher risk with fibrates, hypothyroidism, renal impairment
Check LFTs before and as clinically indicated
Bleeding risk – stop 5–7 days before elective surgery
Omeprazole/esomeprazole (CYP2C19 inhibition – reduced effect; prefer pantoprazole)
Rosuvastatin Calcium: Any time of day; avoid heavy alcohol; separate antacids by 2 hours.
Clopidogrel Bisulphate: With or without food.
Rosuvastatin Calcium: Lipids 4–12 weeks after start then annually; ALT at baseline; CK if muscle symptoms; HbA1c in diabetes-risk patients.
Clopidogrel Bisulphate: Bleeding signs; CBC if TTP suspected.
Rosuvastatin Calcium: No specific treatment; supportive care; monitor LFT and CK. Clopidogrel Bisulphate: Prolonged bleeding; platelet transfusion may restore function.
Supported by component trials: JUPITER (rosuvastatin), CAPRIE and CURE (clopidogrel).
Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness
Do not stop without consulting cardiologist
Prefer pantoprazole if a PPI is needed
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
